svg.title: Clock domains and clock-domain crossings
svg.desc: Two clock domains side by side, each one tinted region with its own color. The core clock domain (ap_clk, 200 MHz, blue) holds the platform adapter, the CSR block, the issue path with the checker and the unit queues, the SPM bridge, the DMA, QACT, the MVM clusters, the scratchpad and one memory arbiter per channel. The control core domain (clk_rv from ap_clk_2, 100 MHz, orange) holds Ibex, the debug module, ITCM, DTCM, the RISC-V bus and the control window. The XRT shell, a gray box at the top, supplies both kernel clocks and resets, each drawn as a line in its domain color, and carries the CSR port and the memory ports into the core domain. Between the two regions, on the boundary, tsr_ctrl_cdc has one synchronizer cell per bundle of crossings, drawn as a pipe that changes color at the cell. From clk_rv to the core clock: the issue FIFO (32 entries of 387 bits, gray pointers), the log FIFO (16 entries of 32 bits), the gray counters ISSUED_SEQ, clk_rv cycles and PERF, the RT_STATE and RT_INFO handshake, and the RV levels and sticky events through two-flop synchronizers. From the core clock to clk_rv: the S, D and MTIME gray counters, the error records (6 of 128 bits, handshake), and the levels. Both ways: the SPM bridge and core window handshake, the LQ and LCQ register handshake, the LOAD handshake into the TCM load port, and the debug-module interface handshake. The reset of the core domain reaches clk_rv through a reset synchronizer. The constraints are ASYNC_REG on the synchronizer flops, a maximum delay equal to the smaller clock period, and a bus skew limit on the gray buses.
